recent_posts.title: Linked and Loaded: Gaijin Single Sign-On Now Available on GeForce NOW
recent_posts.summary: GeForce NOW now supports Gaijin single sign-on, allowing members to link their Gaijin.net account once and launch supported games like War Thunder without repeated logins. The feature is accessible via the GeForce NOW app settings under 'Connections' on PC or Mac. Seven new games have also been added to the platform this week, including Dead as Disco, HUNTDOWN: OVERTIME, Nuclear Option, Sintopia, Kiln, Hotel Architect, and PowerWash Simulator 2, all playable with RTX 5080 performance for Ultimate members.

recent_posts.title: NVIDIA Spectrum-X — the Open, AI-Native Ethernet Fabric — Sets the Standard for Gigascale AI, Now With MRC
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA has announced Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC), a new RDMA transport protocol developed in collaboration with Microsoft, OpenAI, AMD, Broadcom, and Intel, now released as an open specification through the Open Compute Project. MRC enables a single RDMA connection to distribute traffic across multiple network paths, improving throughput, load balancing, and resilience for large-scale AI training clusters. Deployed on NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet hardware, MRC provides hardware-speed failure detection and rerouting in microseconds, sustains high GPU utilization under congestion, and supports multiplanar network designs scaling to hundreds of thousands of GPUs. Major deployments include OpenAI's Blackwell generation clusters, Microsoft's Fairwater data center, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure's Abilene facility.

recent_posts.title: NVIDIA and ServiceNow Partner on New Autonomous AI Agents for Enterprises
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA and ServiceNow are expanding their enterprise AI partnership, announced at ServiceNow Knowledge 2026. Key highlights include Project Arc, a self-evolving autonomous desktop agent for knowledge workers built on NVIDIA OpenShell (an open-source secure runtime for sandboxed agent execution), and ServiceNow AI Control Tower for governance. The collaboration also covers NVIDIA agent skills and Nemotron open models for customizable enterprise workflows, NOWAI-Bench for benchmarking enterprise AI agents, and NVIDIA Blackwell-powered AI factories delivering 50x greater token output per watt than Hopper for cost-efficient at-scale deployment.

recent_posts.title: How enterprises can deploy long-running autonomous AI agents with NemoClaw
recent_posts.summary: OpenClaw, a self-hosted persistent AI agent framework, reached 250,000 GitHub stars in 60 days, surpassing React. Unlike prompt-triggered AI, OpenClaw 'claws' run continuously on a heartbeat cycle, autonomously completing tasks and escalating only decisions requiring human input. NVIDIA is collaborating with OpenClaw's creator to improve security and has released NemoClaw — a reference implementation combining OpenClaw, the OpenShell sandboxed runtime, and NVIDIA Nemotron models with hardened defaults for enterprise deployment. Use cases span financial monitoring, drug discovery, IT operations, and engineering simulation. Key governance priorities include auditable open-source code, sandboxed runtime permissions, and local compute via DGX Spark to keep sensitive data on-premises. Each AI wave multiplies inference demand: autonomous agents drive roughly 1,000x more token usage than reasoning AI.

recent_posts.title: GeForce NOW adds 16 games in May with expanded RTX 5080 cloud performance
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA GeForce NOW is adding 16 games to its cloud gaming library in May 2026, including day-one launches of Forza Horizon 6 and 007 First Light. Ultimate membership now defaults to RTX 5080-class virtual rigs across nearly the entire Ready-to-Play library, enabling up to 5K at 120fps or 360fps at 1080p, with DLSS 4, NVIDIA Reflex, and advanced ray tracing. The service is also celebrating 30 years of Firaxis by adding classic titles like XCOM 2 and Civilization: Beyond Earth as Install-to-Play titles, alongside a Steam sale with up to 90% off Firaxis games.

recent_posts.title: NVIDIA Launches Nemotron 3 Nano Omni Model, Unifying Vision, Audio and Language for up to 9x More Efficient AI Agents
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA has launched Nemotron 3 Nano Omni, an open multimodal model that unifies vision, audio, and language capabilities in a single 30B-A3B hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture. Unlike agentic systems that chain separate models for each modality, this model eliminates the need for separate perception models, delivering up to 9x higher throughput than comparable open omni models. It tops six leaderboards for document intelligence, video, and audio understanding. Use cases include computer use agents, document intelligence, and audio-video reasoning. The model is available with open weights on Hugging Face, OpenRouter, and NVIDIA's NIM microservice platform, and is already being adopted by companies including H Company, Palantir, and Foxconn.

recent_posts.title: Into the Omniverse: Manufacturing’s Simulation-First Era Has Arrived
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA's simulation-first approach to manufacturing is gaining traction through OpenUSD and the Omniverse platform. The SimReady content standard enables physically accurate 3D assets to move reliably across rendering, simulation, and AI training pipelines. Real-world results include ABB Robotics achieving 99% sim-to-real accuracy with up to 80% reduction in commissioning time, JLR compressing 4-hour aerodynamic simulations to 1 minute using neural surrogate models trained on 20,000+ CFD runs, and Tulip's Factory Playback platform delivering a projected 3% yield increase and 10% rework reduction at Terex. Resources for developers to get started with Isaac Sim, Omniverse libraries, and the SimReady Foundation specification are provided.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI’s New GPT-5.5 Powers Codex on NVIDIA Infrastructure — and NVIDIA Is Already Putting It to Work
recent_posts.summary: NVIDIA has deployed OpenAI's new GPT-5.5 model through the Codex agentic coding app to over 10,000 employees across all departments. The model runs on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack-scale systems, which deliver 35x lower cost per million tokens and 50x higher token output per second per megawatt versus prior-generation hardware. NVIDIA IT provisioned dedicated cloud VMs for each employee with a zero-data retention policy and read-only production access for security. The rollout reflects a decade-long NVIDIA-OpenAI partnership that began with Jensen Huang hand-delivering the first DGX-1 to OpenAI in 2016, and now includes OpenAI committing to deploy over 10 gigawatts of NVIDIA systems for future AI infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: GeForce NOW adds Xbox Game Pass and Ubisoft+ in-app labels plus six new games
recent_posts.summary: GeForce NOW has launched new in-app labels that make it easy to identify which games in the library belong to connected subscription services like Xbox Game Pass and Ubisoft+. Six new games are now available on the platform, headlined by Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard. GeForce NOW Premium members also get early access to a Thor Midgard Umber Skin in Marvel Rivals, claimable through April 24 for free-tier members and redeemable until May 23.

recent_posts.title: Making Sense of the Early Universe
recent_posts.summary: Astronomer Brant Robertson at UC Santa Cruz is using NVIDIA GPUs and AI to process the massive datasets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope. His team built an AI pipeline including Morpheus, a semantic segmentation model that classifies galaxies pixel-by-pixel, and GalaxyFriends, a UMAP-based tool for organizing ~90,000 galaxies by similarity. Key findings include unexpectedly early disk galaxies that challenged existing cosmological models. The team also applies AI techniques similar to NVIDIA DLSS to remove atmospheric blur from ground-based telescope images, preparing for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory which will generate ~20TB of data nightly. All datasets covering nearly 500,000 galaxies are released publicly.

top_posts.title: Elon Musk Gets Just-Launched NVIDIA DGX Spark: Petaflop AI Supercomputer Lands at SpaceX
top_posts.summary: NVIDIA launched DGX Spark, a desktop-sized AI supercomputer delivering one petaflop of performance with 128GB unified memory, capable of running models up to 200 billion parameters locally. CEO Jensen Huang personally delivered the first unit to Elon Musk at SpaceX's Starbase facility. The system targets developers, researchers, and creators who need supercomputer-class AI performance in a portable form factor, with general availability starting October 15, 2025.

top_posts.title: 2024 AI Predictions
top_posts.summary: Enterprises are expected to harness the power of generative AI in 2024 to revolutionize productivity, innovation, and creativity. Customized generative AI applications using proprietary data will become more common in businesses. Open-source pretrained models will be combined with private or real-time data to accelerate productivity and cost benefits. Off-the-shelf AI models will be customized using AI microservices. Collaboration among AI organizations will lead to the development of standardized AI safety protocols. The automotive industry will utilize generative AI for design, shopping experiences, and AV development. Networking efficiency and performance will be emphasized in order to support accelerated computing with GPUs. The financial services industry will adopt an AI-first approach. Physics-ML will be used in energy companies to accelerate simulations and enhance decision-making. LLMs and generative AI will play a significant role in robotics programming and simulation development.

top_posts.title: Wired for Action: Langflow Enables Local AI Agent Creation on NVIDIA RTX PCs
top_posts.summary: Langflow enables users to create AI agents locally on NVIDIA RTX PCs through a visual drag-and-drop interface, eliminating the need for coding expertise. By integrating with Ollama, users can run AI workflows entirely offline with benefits including data privacy, no API costs, and GPU-accelerated performance. The platform supports advanced use cases like travel planning agents and Notion automation, while new integrations with RTX Remix and Project G-Assist expand capabilities for game modding and system control through natural language commands.

top_posts.title: Denmark Launches Leading Sovereign AI Supercomputer to Solve Scientific Challenges With Social Impact
top_posts.summary: Denmark has launched its largest AI supercomputer, Gefion, aimed at solving scientific challenges in quantum computing, clean energy, biotechnology, and more. Operated by the Danish Center for AI Innovation with NVIDIA technology, Gefion is designed to enhance national AI capabilities and address global issues such as infectious disease, climate change, and food security. It will support industries, startups, and academic research, driving advancements in areas like computer-aided drug discovery and quantum supremacy.
